Elena Ruiz — Human Factors & Single-Operator Safety said about it: The stopping hold simulation (E34) gives about 161 N tip-hold at a 1.10 m handle, against about 188 N sustained hold and about 209 N pull in the climb simulation (E23), and I take from the 8 <strong>ERGONOMICS</str (E28) that International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 11228-2 recommends for 90 percent of people two-handed sustained push 230 N for men and 130 N for women and sustained pull 240 N for men and 140 N for women.
Kenji Tanaka — Stair-Climbing Locomotion said about it: Without the lock the hand must still meet the climb simulation (E23) at about 209 N pull and about 188 N hold, so I confirm what Elena Ruiz takes from the ergonomics push-pull guidance (E28) on sustained limits and from the parking-brake rule for trucks to 500 kg (E30): release must mean locked.
